properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EXPAND OPER LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/27/2026
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8265640
Permit API: 015-23981
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wysox Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/27/2026
Comments: On 02/26/2025 Expand representative Steven Moyer reported a discovered release onsite. He stated "there was a hole in containment. They picked up the containment around 1100 hours that morning. An unknown amount of frack water mixed with stormwater on pad. Creston Environmental will be conducting the cleanup." On 02/27/2026 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident response inspection of the Wygrala Well Pad in Wysox Township, Bradford County. The weather was 30 degrees and sunny. I arrived at 0915 hours. Upon arrival to the site DEP met with Expand representative Danielle Schadd and two Creston Environmental representatives. The area of the reported release is estimated to be an area of 75x150. There were barricades in place to keep the area closed off to vehicles (photo #2). Within the 75x150 area the elevated conductivity of the soil varies between 0-4 mS/cm. There were no pooled fluids within the reported release area. Approximately 2-3 inches of material had already been excavated and placed into containment onsite. Alderdice, Inc. was onsite removing the material during the inspection. Creston Environmental was conducting further testing during the inspection. They were going to expand their testing area due to the ground thawing with increased temperatures. The cause of the release was due to a ripped seam in the pad wide containment. This caused freshwater and brine mixture to leak through onto the pad surface. The same pad wide containment was in place during stimulation (01/23/2026-02/12/2926) and drill out (02/15/2026-02/18/2026). The quantity of the release is unknown. Due to the unknown quantity of the release this is being referred to ECB for Act 2 compliance.Based on the reported release (CTS #395411) the following violations have been cited against API #015-23981:CSL 402(b)35 P.S. 6018.301 SWMA25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)I departed at 1000 hours.

Comments: The Department of Environmental (DEP) conducted a Follow-up Inspection of the Tilden Marcellus - Thomas 808 well pad located in Elk Twp, Tioga Co. on 6/12/2019 @1000 hours. The weather was rain 62 degrees. Present onsite for the inspection was Ross McMann, DEP Geologic Specialist and myself. Activity onsite consisted of Tilden Marcellus conducting stimulation activities on the 4H well. The DEP was onsite to follow-up on remediation activities associated with the 6/3/2019 release of an estimate 10 barrels of stimulation fluid outside containment. As of today's inspection, a lined ditch was observed installed across the ESE fill slope of the well pad. The ditch was collecting potentially impacted runoff from the well pad. Fluid in the ditch had a field measured conductivity of 460uS/cm. The E&S control at the base of the SE fill slope was observed full of fluid with a field measured conductivity of 420uS/cm. A pump was positioned, on containment, just upslope of the E&S control to remove water as needed. Onsite personnel stated no elevated conductivity fluid has been observed in the E&S control. Fluid along the ESE edge of the well pad had a field measured conductivity of 10.45mS/cm indicating the continued presence of a pollutional substance. Soils just off the edge of the well pad had elevated conductivity of >2.0mS/cm in the upper inch of soil. Onsite personnel stated once stimulation activities were complete, Tilden would initiate removal of the containment/rig mats, screening of the E/SE section of the pad (and surrounding areas), and removal of all impacted material. Onsite personnel were notified of any deficiencies. Violations, cited 6/4/2019 in IR#2889847, remain OUTSTANDING against the 3H well, API#117-20476. No other violations are noted at this time. We departed the site @1200 hours.

Comments: On 6/15/26 at 11:29 AM, I arrived at the Kovalish 1 in Derry Twp, Westmoreland county. The department performed a follow up inspection of the KOVALISH 1 OG well. Permit number# 129-24618. At the time of inspection: The well is considered abandoned and was observed shut in and disconnected. Violations 78.91(a) and OGA3220(A) are being continued. And all the necessary equipment for production remains removed from the site. The disconnected electrical service and the disconnected associated pipelines that are exposed make the site appear to have had an electric powered gas compressor on location sometime ago. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/12/2024 to FARRINGTON & HEPLER GAS & OIL INC in Washington Township, Jefferson county. 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.

Report Details

Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8201062
Permit API: 065-26269
Unconventional: No
County: Jefferson
Municipality: Washington Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/12/2024
Comments: During a routine complete inspection on 5/16/2024 (Inspection Record No. 3788146), I noted API 065-26269 did not have a well tag, equipment not necessary for production was being stored on site, and there was evidence of a production fluid release greater than 42 gallons.During a follow up inspection (FUI) on 6/26/2024 (Inspection Record No. 3790440), I noted the well had a new well tag, the pipe was moved across the access road, and the spill area was seeded and mulched. The Department did not receive a response from the Notice of Violation with the operators intentions to use either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. The Department did not receive tipping receipts or waste manifests associated with removal and disposal of contaminated soil from the spill. The tag violation was closed. The other violations remained open.On a FUI on 8/19/2024 (Inspection Record No. 3816085), I noted the Department still hasn't received tipping receipts or waste manifests regarding the clean up of this site. I emailed Ray Hepler information about Act 2 remediation. On 8/28/2024, Jack Crow, Henry Kramer, Brian Shank and myself met with Ray Hepler at the PA DEP Meadville Regional Office to discuss the outstanding violations at the Wheeler property. Ray Hepler stated he had the contaminated soil from the brine releases on a roll off and would send us the manifests soon. The Department received a manifest for waste on 9/9/2024. However, the manifest stated the soil was "Beaver-PA 100%". The manifest also stated the soil was hauled in a "white pick up truck", but during the 8/28/2024 meeting Ray Hepler stated the soil was in a roll off container. This manifest does not show the proper disposal of the soil from the Wheeler W12 well site located in Jefferson County. Today (9/12/2024), Brian Shank and I conducted a FUI. The pipe not necessary for production was still being stored near the access road. The spill area appeared to have new top soil and grass seed. We collected soil conductivity readings throughout the spill area. A background soil conductivity reading was collected. The soil conductivity reading was 154.5 pS/cm. Near the production tank, the soil conductivity reading was 3.28 mS/cm. Approximately 4 feet from the production tank, the soil conductivity reading 1416 pS/cm. These readings indicate that the prior spill has not been remediated yet. We collected grab soil samples to send to the Department's accredited laboratory. The samples will be analyzed for SAC 960 and UVIR.The outstanding violations for the Wheeler W12 well site will remain open at this time.

Comments: On June 2, 2020, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident inspection as a response to a reported production fluid spill at Beech Resources Premier Pad. DEP received a phone call from Don Stevenson with Beech Resources reporting a spill of around 400 gallons of production fluid from the GPU onsite. A dump line valve on the GPU recently failed and was replaced. Within the next couple days vegetation downslope from the GPU was noticed to be dead. How the production fluid was spilled is still being determined. At the time of the inspection, the operator was in the process of excavating the impacted soil. There are two strips of impacted soil, they are about equal in size. The impacted area is about 10 ft wide by 90 ft long. At the top of the slope, the excavator had dug up about 3 ft deep of soil. Soil conductivity in the right strip of dead vegetation ranged from 700 uS/cm to over range readings of the meter, which is 4,000 uS/cm. The impacted soil is still within the LOD so no production fluid left the permitted LOD. Beech Resources plans to follow the Act 2 remediation. The spill of production fluid outside of containment is a violation of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), §78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. Outstanding violations from Inspection No. 3001824 still remain.

Comments: This site located in a grassy field west off Parks Road at the end of a short access, 320' west of residence and the spring used for their water supply. Well set-up for production with a separator, drip and 100 barrel tank in secondary containment. Annual electronic production report submitted through 2023. Water in the hole excavated northwest of the secondary containment was tested with handheld conductivity meter, the reading was over 4 milli Siemens. Water pooled in the hole where the secondary containment was excavated was ~2 milli siemens. You are hereby requested to continue to follow Department Policy 800-5000-001, Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil and Gas Well Sites or Access Road. This Policy sets forth the procedures that should be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release noted in this Notice of Violation by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process.

SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/27/2023
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8166300
Permit API: 081-20763
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Lewis Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/27/2023
Comments: On November 27, 2023, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident inspection at the Range Resources Cornwall Mountain 1-8H. This is to follow up with a reported spill by Range Resources on the afternoon of November 25, 2023 of approximately a barrel of production fluid. The production fluid was noticed bubbling from the well pad surface in the area of the buried dump line for the GPUs. The buried dump line from GPU 4 was immediately isolated. Range Resources found a small hole in the the buried dump line from the GPU to the production fluid tanks during the initial excavation where the bubbling was occurring. Upon arrival, Range Resources had dug three pilot holes along the dump line to aid in delineating the extent of the impact from the hole in the line. Three more pilot holes were dug during the inspection moving toward the production fluid tanks. The pilot holes were dug by a mobile high vacuum system. The last pilot hole dug, closest to the production fluid tanks, had a soil conductivity of less than 1,000 uS/cm. Range Resources conducted screening of the soil conductivity of the pilot holes and the conductivity ranged from less than 1,000 uS/cm to 4,650 uS/cm. Range Resources said that the production fluid that spilled seemed to follow the path of the dump line from the GPUs and did not appear to leave the well pad. DEP did not observe any seeps or erosion off the well pad edge indicating the production fluid had left the well pad. Kirby Steck with Range Resources said with digging the pilot holes they now know the extent of the area they need to excavate along the dump line. Range Resources plans to begin excavating the area around the GPU dump line to remove the impacted soil. The impacted soil will be placed in a roll off dumpster which was in containment. Once the area has been excavated, Range Resources plans on contacting Moody and Associates to collect the Act 2 confirmatory soil samples. The spilling of production fluid outside of containment onto the well pad surface cause violations of the Clean Stream Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act 301.

Comments: This well was inspected as part of an on going stray gas migration case involving gas migrating into a private water supply (CTS#373559).¿¿ ¿¿ ¿¿ The well head and casing strings were observed at the time of inspection for leaks, deterioration, and possible failures.¿¿ As part of the investigation 1 slam bar hole approximately 1-2 feet from the well head was placed into the ground to identify if any methane was migrating from the well bore.¿¿3% LEL was detected in this slam bar hole. At this time, the Department is requesting an investigation into the possible source of methane to be conducted by the operator.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/09/2024
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8182510
Permit API: 081-21941
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Plunketts Creek Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/09/2024
Comments: Site inspection conducted to inspect 13,000 barrel Modular Aboveground Storage Structure (MASS) and site secondary containment. Meeting on site today with EQT Company Man Matt Casler. Weather conditions are sunny and 59 degrees F.According to Mr. Casler, Next Tier is on site conducting hydraulic fracturing operations for nine wells at the Mallory A Pad. The crew is zipper fracking four wells at time of inspection (1H, 3H, 5H, 17H). Pressure testing is under way for the 3H well ahead of the next pumping stage. Three wells are now complete and two wells are yet to be started. Approximately 190 stages are left for stimulation among the remaining wells. The remaining work is expected to take about three weeks. During this inspection, the Department observed secondary containment and berms which appear to be functioning as designed. All fluid transfer lines from the off load area(photo 6) to the MASS appear to be in good condition and no leaks or spills were observed. Fresh gravel is in place near areas remediated from earlier spills. Puddled fluid and damp soils on the pad were screened for elevated electrical conductivity during this inspection. Meter readings were observed to be less than 1mS/cm on pad rock surface adjacent to the main secondary containment structure and the MASS. There are no new violations noted.The Department requests EQT provide containment inspection and repair logs for dates 3/19/24-4/9/24 to juabbott@pa.gov. Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21938 for the 3/1/24 produced fluid release and against permit 081-21941 for the 12/21/23 produced fluid release. The violations will remain outstanding until attainment of Act 2 remediation standards.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: WILMOTH INTERESTS INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/23/2025
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8253360
Permit API: 123-48915
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sheffield Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/23/2025
Comments: A production equipment malfunction at the ANF 194 49 conventional well resulted in a release of crude oil and produced fluids. The Department was notified of the release by Jason Wells of Wilmoth Interests, Inc. The well was shut in from the gathering lines at the time of the malfunction. Therefore, when the malfunction occurred, downhole pressure released vertically from the well head causing crude oil to be sprayed a significant distance above the well before ultimately settling on the well pad and nearby vegetation. The approximate radius of crude oil laden vegetation and forest understory spans 200 feet in every direction from the well head. It appears that the heaviest aerial migration of the release traveled in a southeast to easterly direction from the well. The exact volume of the release is not immediately quantifiable, but it is clearly in excess of the one barrel limit set forth in the Department's spill policy.The bulk of the fluids released settled on the well pad. At the time of this inspection, 3-4 inches of crude oil and produced fluids were present on the pad near the well head. Recent rainfall contributed to the volume of liquid present on the pad, and some stormwater runoff was observed to be flowing down the access road berm and onto the pad. The specific conductance of standing fluid on the pad near the flow of stormwater was found to be 6,080 micro Siemens per centimeter. The specific conductance of standing fluid near the well head was found to be in excess of 20,000 micro Siemens per centimeter. No fluids with elevated specific conductance were observed beyond the well pad at the time of this inspection.The crude oil released on the well pad was observed to have migrated beyond the well pad and downslope in a southern direction. The brush barrier downslope of the well pad was heavily coated with crude oil. Pooled crude oil was observed to have migrated beyond the brush barrier on the forest floor and potentially via porous subsurface material. The extent of pooled crude oil visible on the surface of the forest floor was located at a point approximately 180 feet south/southeast of the well pad.Cleanup efforts began immediately after the release was discovered and brought under control. A ditch was excavated along the downslope end of the well pad to provide containment and a means by which to collect pooled fluids with a vac truck. Jason Wells contacted a consulting firm soon after the release with the intent to retain a consultant to oversee the cleanup process for Wilmoth. I spoke with Jason onsite at the time of this inspection to notify him that violations would be included with the inspection report.A Notice of Violations (NOV) is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

Comments: This inspection report has been developed to document an on-site routine complete inspect, and to summarize the overall status of this well and well location. The project was recently acquired by Big Dog Energy, LLC. Applications for the transfer of all three wells permitted on the site, from Geopetro LLC to Big Dog Energy LLC, were received by the Department on August 2, 2021. An application for the transfer of the ESCGP that is currently active on the site was also received by the Department. The current Operator information has not yet been updated in the Department's electronic database. Well number 019-21927, along with two other wells, (API ID#'s: 019-21948, 019-21947), were drilled and currently exist on the location. Although the Act Nine sign has been changed to reflect the current owner of the well location, the well tags have not yet been updated. Updated well tags should be installed on each of the wells at some point in the near future. Inspection ID number's 2092885, 2092888, and 2092893 (conducted on August 17, 2012) suggests that all of the wells have been stimulated. Subsequent inspections have indicated that the wells have been on inactive status since at least December of 2013. ESCGP number ESX11-019-0109 is currently active on the site. The permit was renewed by RE Gas in 2017 and is set to expire on 08/07/2022. None of the earthwork proposed in the plan was ever implemented in the field. Up until very recently, the property owner had been grazing cattle on the site and using the tank pad as a feedlot. A small sediment slide had developed on the cut bank surface to the east of the well location. With the exception of the slide, there are currently no clear E&S or stabilization-related issues associated with the site. Big Dog is currently preparing all of the wells on this site to be placed into production. A contractor hired by Big Dog was working on establishing new barbed wire fencing around the location when this inspection was conducted. Some production equipment, including 3 GPU's are being staged on the site. The slip on the cut surface above the location was discussed with the contractor. Containment under the GPU's was also discussed, as well as updated well tags.

Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/04/2025

Violation ID: 8223439
Permit API: 105-21962
Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter
Municipality: Hector Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/04/2025
Comments: On 03/04/2025 representatives from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Greylock Production LLC's Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 1000 hours, weather was 34F and cloudy. An Act 9 sign is visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).All standing water observed on the pad surface was frozen solid.There are 2 recently completed wells onsite and their American Petroleum Institute (API) numbers are posted at the site entrance; I was unable to confirm if the wells were tagged due to them currently being covered (photos #1 and 2). 2 gas processing units (GPUs) are also located onsite (photo #3). The GPUs are held in a secondary containment structure which did not contain any standing water. There are 4 produced fluid tanks located onsite and stationed in secondary containment (photo #4); the containment structure did not contain any standing water. The tanks were labeled as per the Department's request (photos #5 and 6). A dehydration unit is also noted onsite and held in secondary containment (photo #7).Numerous upright brine tanks and temporary storage tanks are still noted onsite and held in their respective secondary containment structures which appear to be functioning as intended (photos #8 and 9). Multiple lined and covered residual waste containers are in use onsite for ongoing Act 2 remediation efforts as well as disassembly of the pad wide containment system (rig matting) and tear down of completions equipment (photos #10 and 11). The modular aboveground storage structures (MASS) have been removed and the brine offload area has been disassembled (photo #12).Remediation remains ongoing from the releases on 12/04/2024 and 12/09/2024 (Inspection report #'s 3881391 and 3878285) as the areas formerly covered by rig matting and containment structures are now accessible. Pad drainage systems remain shut in to prevent any water from ice and snow melt from leaving the pad. I did not observe any diesel sheen on the pad surface. Water is being removed from the well pad via an onsite vacuum truck as it accumulates. The area located underneath the brine offload area from the release on 12/09/2024 is currently being excavated to comply with Act 2 remediation standards (photo #13). Soil in this area field measured for electrical conductivity at ~1.68mS/cm and fluids accumulating in this area field measured for EC at ~15.67mS/cm (photos #14 and 15). These soils and fluids are being collected via vacuum truck or lined residual waste container.Site stabilization could not be adequately assessed at the time of this inspection due to snow coverage. A weekly erosion and sediment (E and S) inspection log is available for review in the mailbox at the site entrance (photo #16). No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. 1 infiltration basin serves as the site's post construction stormwater management (PCSM) control (photo #17). The basin inlet remains shut in and no fluids or diesel sheen was observed (photo #18). Soil in the basin field measured for EC at ~0.72mS/cm (photo #19).Violations noted in inspection report #'s 3881391 and 3878285 remain outstanding against API #105-21962.No additional violations noted. I departed the site at 1100 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DAKOTA OIL & GAS CO
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/25/2025
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8231588
Permit API: 129-26521
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Upper Burrell Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/25/2025
Comments: On April 25, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Chabal 2 well site in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3965337, where violations were issued in response to an estimated 50 barrel release of a brine/crude oil mixture. No impacts to the Waters of the Commonwealth were observed during the time of IR 3965337.The Department spoke via phone with Penneco representative Marc Jacobs prior to this inspection, who stated that forecasted storms have delayed start of remediation to Monday, 4/28/2025. In response, the impacted area was covered, and oil absorbent booms and E and S controls were installed downslope.The following was observed:The well head is equipped with a well tag appears to be free of fluid leaks at the time of inspection (see photos 2 and 3). The operator's information is posted on the separator (see photo 4). A gas odor was detected onsite during this inspection. The body of the brine tank appears to be sound at the time of inspection (see photos 5 and 6). The path of brown staining that was observed traveling downslope from the brine tank has been covered with plastic sheeting in preparation for the forecasted rains. Additional oil absorbent booms have also been placed down slope of the covered impacted area (see photos 8-15). No evidence of visual impacts and/or elevated conductivity were detected down slope of impacted area (see photos 16 and 17).Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that the impacted area has been adequately,protected to mitigate risk of the impact being spread by stormwater.Violations issued from IR 3965337 shall remain outstanding.

Comments: This well was inspected as part of an on going gas migration case. At the time of inspection I observed a cable rig rigged up over the well and the well shut in. There was an odor of gas emitting from the well and I could visually see gas bubbling behind the tubing at surface. A slam bar hole was placed 1.5' from the well and was metered with and ALTAIR 5X five sensor meter. At this slam bar hole 100% methane was detected. I then put a series of slam bar holes (12 total) radiating outward from the well. At points 50' from the well no gas was detected. I spoke with Justin Hanson of Bull Run Energy who does all the well tending in this area for Armac and he stated that they were going to run a cement bond log on this well tomorrow (03/14/2023).

Comments: On September 23, 2025, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Apollo Resource's Whyel 1 Well located in Nicholson Township, Fayette County following violations issued under inspection report 3875658. IR 4055015 documents an Operator response the Department received which states: "Apollo Resources LLC is responding to an inspection report on Wyhel Well 37-051-23812. Apollo Resources had installed new valves on the annulus of the well. We will do a soil probe of the site and assess if soil needs to be removed as prior when valves were installed there wasn't evidence of any large spill."At the time of this inspection a well posting was observed on a production tank with all required information posted on it. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from the production tank. At the time of this inspection, the Department did not observe any active fluid leaks or discharges from the annulus which is the location of the previously observed dripping/leaking, it appears work was done to cease the fluid leak. Conductivity readings were taken in the area below the annulus (0.1806 mS and 0.1547 mS) and were compared to a background soil conductivity reading taken in some vegetation adjacent to the well site (0.1325 mS). These soil conductivity readings are comparable to the background soil conductivity reading, however, the Operator has yet to provide the Department with the following: -an incident report, how the Operator quantified the amount spilled and the waste manifest from the site remediation be upon its receipt.The Department is again requesting the Operator provide the Department with the aforementioned documents. Based on today's inspection, violations shall remain outstanding pending the receipt of the aforementioned documents.

The Department recommends sucking up this fluid as much as possible. The pad surface underneath this secondary containment, to the extent that can be seen, appears to still be damp. On Pad A, six wells are staged for production. Six GPUs are present within secondary containment. A battery of frac tanks is present within secondary containment. The tanks and containment appear to be in good condition. No issues noted on Pad A.Violations remain outstanding for the June 24, 2022 release.

Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/26/2024
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8212036
Permit API: 113-20366
Unconventional: Yes
County: Sullivan
Municipality: Forks Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/26/2024
Comments: Arrived onsite in response to a release of produced fluid that occurred on 12/25/24. I spoke with Mike Demming (CHK) during the inspection. The release occurred due to produced fluid freezing in a pipe on a filter pot. The burst pipe allowed the produced fluid to spray onto the pad and into the production tank secondary containment.The impacted area of the pad was estimated to be 80' by 12'. The volume of fluid released was estimated to be between 1.5 and 2 barrels based on the fluid levels in the affected equipment. Conductivity readings were taken by CHK both on the pad surface and directly from the broken pipe. The conductivity readings were at or below 1 milliesiemen per centimeter (mS/cm). There was some black material that was released with the produced fluid.The pad surface was covered by snow and ice and did not appeared to be directly impacted. The impacted snow and frozen produced fluid were removed and placed into the production tank secondary containment. The resulting fluid in secondary containment will be removed and properly disposed of as weather permits.CHK stated that they will peruse Act 2 remediation for the release. Creston was onsite collecting Act 2 confirmation samples and screening to ensure complete removal of impacted materials. The samples will be analyzed for brine and oil contents due to the black coloring. There did not appear to be any impacts beyond those identified on the pad.The result of this inspection Violations Noted for 78a56(a) and CSL 402(b).
